title: A partitioner written with Math.abs sends one key in two billion to a negative partition
summary: A custom Kafka partitioner routes a tenant's records by the hash of its id, so that every record of a tenant lands on the same partition. A developer rewrites Kafka's `toPositive(hash) % n`, with its unexplained bit mask, as `Math.abs(hash) % n`, which says what it means. The module's properties file says every hash lands on a partition of the topic. The prover finds the one `int` whose absolute value is negative, and the tool replays it: the partition is negative, which the producer rejects, and that tenant's records are never sent.

change.description: Replace `(hash & 0x7fffffff) % numPartitions` with `Math.abs(hash) % numPartitions`. The mask is there to make the hash positive, and `Math.abs` is the name for that. The tests pass: positive hashes spread as before, and negative hashes land on a partition.

risk: `Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE)` is `Integer.MIN_VALUE`, because `2^31` does not fit in an `int`. The remainder is then negative, the producer throws `IllegalArgumentException: Invalid partition given with record` on every send for that key, and the tenant whose id hashes to `MIN_VALUE` loses every record, silently if the send is asynchronous and the callback only logs. Nothing else is affected, so dashboards stay green: this is the kind of bug that surfaces as a single customer's complaint months later, with a hash that nobody thinks to check. Kafka's own `Utils.toPositive` has the mask precisely because of this; the Javadoc of `Math.abs` warns about it in its last sentence.
explanation: The property reads: for every `numPartitions > 0`, the result is in `[0, numPartitions)`. JBMC searches small values first and finds nothing, because the bug needs one specific hash out of 2^32. The next pass covers the whole domain and finds it: `hash = -2147483648`. The tool replays the method on that input and reports a negative partition number. A test could have included this value, but only if its author knew the one fact the cleanup forgot; the property states what every partitioner must do, and the prover checks it against every hash.
resolution: Keep the mask, or use `Math.floorMod(hash, numPartitions)`, which is defined for negative dividends. The property stays in the file, so the next rewrite of this line is checked against every `int` again.
notes: `Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE)` is negative: one key in two billion goes to a negative partition.

Gap scan (step 1a of `llm-dlc/loops/sound-verdicts.md`, 5 November 2026, JDK 25.0.4.1, from the bytecode, nothing proved): the tool's own checker meets no gap in the 1 method the proof reaches, so strict mode does not move this verdict. The recorded proof is JBMC's, which strict mode of the tool's own checker does not change. JBMC's own approximations are step 4c's.
provenance: Constructed from the `Math.abs(x) % n` partitioning bug, which recurs in custom Kafka partitioners and in hash-based sharding generally; Kafka's `Utils.toPositive` exists because of it.

references.title: Kafka, Utils.toPositive (the mask, with the comment that explains it)
Java API, Math.abs(int): "if the argument is equal to the value of Integer.MIN_VALUE, the result is that same value, which is negative"
